# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-14 (Extended v119)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to 1826. **Current narrative point (Summer Year 4, late afternoon ~5:30 P.M., 30 minutes until trap springs at 6 P.M.)**: Paris—Gorbeau house (50-52, Salpêtrière district); Luxembourg gardens; le Petit-Picpus convent; M. Gillenormand's residences; English provincial towns (Dunstead, Staveford, Kelmere, Torton, Ostcombe, Ravenmere, Kelford, Yarlby, Gulhaven, Wilwick); various streets (Rue Gracieuse, Rue Pierre-Lombard, etc.). **Environmental**: Spring—frost silvering hedges, smoke flat; Summer—warm air, sparrows, bees, gulls quarrying, salt/tar scent; Autumn/Winter transition—icy breeze, snow falling; **Current (late afternoon, Summer Year 4)**: Snow ceased then resumed, day declining, roads rutted/puddled after thaw, light early, baker's boy late, line at oven long, cart with turnips passed well, bell for vespers ringing thinly, gulls quarreling over fish heads, wind off water carries salt/tar, dog barking then quiet, crooked sun chalked on wall.

## Primary Locations
**GORBEAU HOUSE**: 50-52 Salpêtrière district. **JONDRETTE DEN**: Within Gorbeau; abject, fetid, sordid. Furniture: straw chair, infirm table, crockery, two pallets, straw beds. Walls: leprous, seamed, scars, obscene charcoal sketches, repulsive moisture. Fireplace with brazier filled burning charcoal (glowing hot, red with blue flame), pot, broken boards, suspended rags, bird-cage, ashes. Dormer window (four broken panes draped spiders' webs). Colored engraving "THE DREAM" (black frame): sleeping woman/child, eagle with crown, Napoleon on blue column. Wooden panel against wall, picture-face turned to wall (now turned to reveal coarse daub/principal personage harsh foreign canvas style). Two heaps: old iron and ropes (actually well-made rope-ladder with wooden rungs and two hooks). Verdigris candlestick with burning candle providing sole light (brazier concealed behind old screen). **Current state (late afternoon)**: Illuminated by candle; crockery and chimney pieces casting large shadows. Calm, threatening, hideous atmosphere anticipating something terrible.

## Jean Valjean and Cosette
Valjean integrated as convent assistant gardener; inhabits old garden hut with Fauchelevent. Spiritual transformation complete. Cosette became convent scholar; believes Valjean is her father; adores him. Fauchelevent sole ally aware of full presence. **Present state (Summer Year 4)**: Cosette about thirteen/fourteen years old; appeared in Jondrette hovel as charitable visitor with M. Leblanc distributing charity.

## Javert's Pursuit
Attached to Paris police after Valjean's escape. **Status (Summer Year 4, present)**: Tall man, square face, thin firm mouth, thick gray ferocious whiskers; glance searches rather than penetrates; terrifying and reassuring simultaneously. **Action (present, late afternoon Summer Year 4)**: Received report from Marius Pontmercy regarding Jondrette ambush plot. Gave Marius two small steel pistols loaded with two balls each. Instructed Marius: hide in chamber to appear departed, watch through hole in wall, fire shot when matters reach crisis (not too soon), let men proceed toward execution then intervene. Javert entered terrible hovel in Rue Gracieuse (quarter-hour), purchased large cold chisel from Rue Pierre-Lombard ironmonger, proceeded to Rue du Petit-Banquier vicinity, sprang across wall and disappeared (planning ambush position).

## Marius Pontmercy: Development, Passion, and Crisis

**Identity and age**: Baron Marius Pontmercy, twenty years old; three years since left grandfather. **Paternal legacy**: Colonel's written instruction regarding baron title and Waterloo sergeant Thénardier. Lost medallion of black shagreen.

**Political evolution (Winter Year 3 → Spring Year 4)**: Converted to Bonapartism and republicanism; political fevers dissipated through reverie; Revolution of 1830 calmed views. Sympathies to humanity over nation, woman over people, idea over deed.

**Material condition (Spring Year 4)**: Gorbeau cabinet 30 francs annually; sustenance 20 sous daily (365 francs yearly); clothing 100 francs; linen 100 francs. Total: 450 francs. Earned approximately 700 francs yearly. **Refused advancement (Winter Year 3)**: M. Magimel offered 1,500 francs annually—Marius refused to preserve liberty and dignity. Deliberately stopped working to dedicate time to thought.

**Grandfather quarrel**: Violent estrangement three years ago without rapprochement. Grandfather's suffering locked within breast.

**Relationship with Friends of the A B C**: Met Courfeyrac; became good friends. Cordial with group but did not enter decidedly. Close to **M. Mabeuf**—owed him revolution within soul. **Social activities (Spring Year 4)**: Dined with Courfeyrac; breakfasted at Café Voltaire.

## The Mysterious Couple, Girl (Cosette), and Marius's Passion

**Initial six-month observation (over one year prior)**: Marius noticed man approximately sixty (M. Leblanc) and very young girl on Luxembourg bench daily. Man: retired military officer, robust, weary, kindly. Girl: thin, awkward, promise of handsome eyes; wore convent scholar dress.

**Six-month interruption**: Observation ceased.

**Reunion and girl's transformation (Summer Year 3)**: Girl became well-dressed young maiden; wore black damask dress, white crape bonnet, white gloves, carved Chinese ivory parasol handle, silken shoe.

**Marius's indifference (Summer Year 3)**: Found only child's glance; paid no further attention.

**First meaningful glance and awakening (Spring Year 4)**: Their glances met on warm day. Marius perceived he wore everyday clothes; resolved to dress differently. Following day wore new coat, seated himself surveying her. His worship of his father retreated to depths of soul.

**Marius's emotional transformation**: Love came. Brain felt on fire. She appeared beautiful, wholly feminine and angelic. Vexed about dust on boots. Walked like madman; ate and spoke excitedly; laughed uproariously.

**Strategic approach (Spring Year 4)**: Combined stations behind trees/pedestals with diplomacy. Sometimes remained motionless half-hour in shade. She bent upon Marius all reveries of virginal and passionate eye.

**M. Leblanc's response**: Noticed something. Often rose when Marius arrived and moved to bench by Gladiator. Marius did not pursue. M. Leblanc stared intently at Marius.

**Escalation and handkerchief (Spring Year 4)**: Found handkerchief on bench. Very simple, white, fine, perfumed. Marked U. F. Marius thought "Ursule!" Kissed handkerchief, placed on heart during day, beneath lips at night.

**Leg incident and jealousy (Spring Year 4)**: **May breeze lifted dress to height of garter. A leg of exquisite shape appeared. Marius saw it. He was exasperated and furious.** Girl hastily thrust down dress with divinely troubled motion. Marius determined to be vexed. **Harsh and capricious jealousy of the flesh awakened in his heart.** When she passed bench, Marius darted sullen and ferocious glance. She gave slight straightening with backward movement: "Well, what is the matter?"

**Veteran encounter and paroxysm**: A bent, wrinkled, pale veteran in Louis XV uniform bearing soldier's cross crossed walk. Marius perceived he had satisfied air; struck him aged cynic addressed him fraternal wink. **Marius reached paroxysm of jealousy.** "Perhaps he was there! Perhaps he saw!"

**M. Leblanc and girl's disappearance (Summer-Autumn Year 4)**: Summer passed, autumn came, winter arrived. Neither returned to Luxembourg. **Marius had but one thought—to gaze once more on that sweet and adorable face.** Fell into black melancholy. All was over. Work disgusted him; walking tired him.

**Self-reproach (Autumn Year 4)**: Heaped hundred reproaches on himself. Confided nothing to Courfeyrac, but Courfeyrac guessed everything.

**Ball at Sceaux (September Year 4)**: Allowed himself taken to ball hoping to find her. Did not see her. Left friends, returned home on foot alone through night, weary, feverish, with sad and troubled eyes.

**Miraculous rediscovery and action (Summer Year 4, afternoon)**: **Marius perceived the girl (Cosette) in Jondrette hovel when she arrived with M. Leblanc to distribute charity.** "It was certainly she. Marius could hardly distinguish her through the luminous vapor which had suddenly spread before his eyes. It was that sweet, absent being, that star which had beamed upon him for six months." **Marius shuddered in dismay, felt on brink of bursting into tears.** His heart palpitated; seemed to him he had lost his soul and just found it again. During entire visit, Marius lived in ecstasy; eyes remained fixed on girl; heart seized and wholly enveloped her. Did not know sound of her voice. **He devoured her with his eyes. Could not believe divine creature was in midst of vile creatures in that monstrous lair. Seemed to him he beheld humming-bird in midst of toads.**

## The Jondrette Family and Ambush Plot—Present Crisis

**Current time: ~5:30 P.M., trap springs at 6 P.M.—30 minutes remaining.**

**Scheme and principals**: Jondrette arranged ambush. M. Leblanc will arrive at 6 o'clock to bring sixty francs (claimed as landlord payment). Accomplices include Panchaud (alias Printanier, alias Bigrenaille) and other prowlers. **Preparation state (late afternoon)**: Brazier with charcoal glowing hot and red, blue flame flickering. Chisel heated in brazier. Two heaps prepared: old iron and rope-ladder. Jondrette allowed pipe to go out (sign of preoccupation); sat examining long kitchen knife from drawer, tested edge on nail, returned knife to drawer. Jondrette woman dressed in black bonnet with plumes (like heralds-at-arms coronation hats), immense tartan shawl, man's shoes. Jondrette instructed: light lantern, stand behind lower door, open instantly when carriage stops, light staircase and corridor, go downstairs quickly, pay coachman, dismiss fiacre.

**Four additional accomplices (present)**: One old man (white hair contrasting with blackened face) leaning against wall, eyes closed, appearing asleep. Two young men (one bearded, one long-haired). One standing near door-post. All four with bare arms, faces smeared with black, no shoes, some barefooted. Seated motionless on beds except one at door-post.

**Marius's position (present, ~5:30 P.M.)**: Seated on his bed in adjoining chamber. Gave his key to Javert (inspector). Pistols (two small steel, each loaded with two balls) concealed in trousers pockets. Cannot yet follow or warn M. Leblanc without exposing himself. Awaiting signal moment to fire shot. Experiences indescribable anxiety; hears beating of arteries like ticking watch in dark. Reflects on double march—crime advancing one side, justice coming other. Not afraid but shudders at what approaches. Entire day produces effect of dream; feels cold barrels of steel pistols to persuade himself not in nightmare. Perceived four men with motionless heads vaguely lighted by remnant of daylight through dormer window. Raised eyes and perceived fifth man (wearing violet knitted vest, old and worn, cotton velvet trousers, wooden shoes, no shirt, bare neck and arms tattooed, face smeared black) who entered so softly door hinges were not heard.

**Scene composition**: Fireplace and two chairs opposite Marius. Brazier concealed by old screen masking chafing-dish. Sole light furnished by candle; smallest crockery casts large shadow. Something indescribably calm, threatening, hideous about chamber. Anticipation of something terrible exists within it.

**Jondrette's monologue**: Engaged in scowls and abrupt unfoldings of right hand as though responding to sombre inward monologue. Talked with apparent incoherence which detracted nothing from thoughtful and sagacious expression of physiognomy. Spoke of happy life with poor darling, wretchedness, arms without work, will without work. Proposed girls learn trade of paper-box makers as simple bread-winner. Lamented fall from days of prosperity. Spoke of one remaining thing: a picture of which he thinks a great deal but willing to part with to live. Rose, went to wall at foot of which stood panel, turned it round still leaving it supported against wall. Really resembled a picture; candle illuminated it somewhat. Marius could make nothing out of it as Jondrette stood between picture and him; only saw coarse daub and principal personage colored with harsh crudity of foreign canvasses and screen paintings.

## Friends of the A B C and Criminal Underground

**Friends of the A B C**: Declared themselves Friends of the A B C—_Abaissé_, the debased (the people). Secret society in embryonic state. Meetings back room Café Musain. Members: Enjolras, Combeferre, Jean Prouvaire, Feuilly, Courfeyrac, Bahorel, Lesgle/Laigle de Meaux, Joly, Grantaire.

**Philosophical discourse on social substructure**: All human societies have subterranean dimensions. Beneath all mines lies deepest stratum—**grave of shadows, cellar of blind, _Inferi_.** Wild spectres roam here, almost beasts, almost phantoms. Two step-mothers: ignorance and misery. From suffering pass to crime. Man becomes dragon. **All others above have one object—suppress it.** So long as society remains what it is, they remain what they are.

**Patron-Minette**: Criminal association members Babet, Gueulemer, Claquesous, Montparnasse. **Gueulemer**: Six feet high, Hercules of no defined position. Lair: sewer of Arche-Marion. **Claquesous**: He was night. Addressed accomplices only in absolute darkness, back turned. Never seen without mask. Ventriloquist. **Function**: Four ruffians formed Proteus, furnish canvas for ambushes in Seine department.

## English Provincial Towns: Rumors and Mundane Activities

**Rumors/claims**: Lurald Stenworth told Thizek Stenenridge deed to Kelmere pastures forged (**confirmed by Lurald telling Ulrald Corrford**). Wenelle Lindmere drowned crossing estuary (rumor, no body). **Dunstead granary fire set on purpose (confirmed: Luena Stenenridge confided to Rozek; Rozek confided to Pewyn Stenenridge)**. Kadan Corrley burned letter from Yera Haskick revealing mill ledger rewritten. Kassa Brackick confided mill ledger rewritten. Fenelle Lindmere confided Stenson family once owed blood debt to Stenenridge family (**later Fenelle told Peten Haskick this**).

**Recent movements**: Peten Haskick packed single trunk and moved from Dunstead to Staveford. Lura followed him to Staveford within the month.

**Mundane activities (Spring-Summer Year 4)**: Volan Stenworth and others read almanac aloud, mispronouncing half saints; bought ribbon at stall and regretted it. Conversations about weather, harvest, lame horse, river up in spring. Lurald laughed at story nobody else found funny. Baker's boy late, line at oven long. Roads rutted and puddled after thaw. Smoke from chimneys lay flat. Lurald spent evening sorting old letters by candlelight. Marald Corrford fell asleep in chair before fire. Nelan Brackick gave Volia Brackick solemn promise to repair roof of chapel at Wilwick. **Current (late afternoon Summer Year 4)**: Marald argued with carter over price of sack of oats. Kassa Brackick asked "Will it rain?"; Lurald Stenworth shrugged. "Price of salt is scandal," said Yewyn Corrford; Yedan agreed. Pewyn Stenenridge asked "Will it rain?"; Kassa shrugged. Yedan walked long way round to avoid muddy square. Fenelle Lindmere read almanac aloud, mispronouncing half saints. Lurald Stenworth mended torn sleeve by window and said little. Ulrald Corrford complained of aching back, as usual. Bremira Corrford complained of aching back, as usual.
